question_en:
The school science festival wants to create a small display board titled "Breakdown of Long Jump Actions." We have the attached excerpt from a collection item. Please answer the following questions:

1. What are the work title, author, production date, and collection number corresponding to the attachment?
2. After locating the complete original plate, number the side-view thumbnails indicated by the header from top to bottom, and left to right within each row, as L01, L02, ... Identify which of these depict "airborne" phases. A phase counts as airborne only if the visible outlines of both feet are separated from the ground line; if either the toe or heel of any foot touches the ground line, or if it cannot be confirmed whether the foot is off the ground, it does not count. List the numbers of all airborne frames, and provide the total count and its proportion to all side-view thumbnails.

Answer Format: Answer by numbered points (1)–(2); use text for both questions. For question 1, provide the four collection details. For question 2, provide the numbers of all airborne frames, the total count, and the proportion.
answer:
(1) Work Title: Jumping, running, broad jump; Author: Eadweard Muybridge; Production Date: 1885-07-06; Collection Number: PG.003856.0130.

(2) The airborne frames are L01, L02, L07, and L08, totaling 4 frames, which accounts for 4/8 of all side-view thumbnails, i.e., 50%.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 8-3-E01

## Step 01 · Extract retrievable identity clues from the local collection excerpt

Action: First examine the local excerpt of the historical original plate provided in the current input; separately record the handwritten title, negative sequence number, and motion pose. Example query: Muybridge "Series Neg. No. 1084" broad jump Smithsonian.

Evidence observation: Clues on the plate include the jumping action, Series Neg. No. 1084, and An. Loc. Serial No. 160. The numbers are clues for locating the same plate; one cannot infer the total count of airborne phases in the entire sequence based solely on a single jumping posture.

Evidence links:
https://www.si.edu/object/nmah_1351934
https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/object/nmah_1351934

Result of this step: Enter the same object record at Smithsonian/NMAH, rather than broadly searching all Muybridge jumping images.

## Step 02 · Verify the object record and evidence availability

Action: Use record number nmah_1351934 to cross-check both the Smithsonian and NMAH portals to verify whether they point to the same collection item.

Evidence observation: In the preserved archival records, direct requests to the two object pages previously returned 403 challenge pages; these challenge pages do not provide valid collection body text. Available fields come from saved snapshots of structured fields and the official IIIF Manifest; proceed with verification based on these materials, without describing the previous request failures as successful access.

Evidence links:
https://www.si.edu/object/nmah_1351934
https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/object/nmah_1351934
https://ids.si.edu/ids/manifest/SIA-2004-44757

Result of this step: Use the official Manifest to verify the title, author, date, and collection number.

## Step 03 · Read the four metadata items from the official Manifest

Action: In the metadata list, search by label for Title, Maker, Date made, and ID Number; do not confuse Catalog number or Accession number with the collection number required by the question.

Evidence observation: Title=Jumping, running, broad jump; Maker=Muybridge, Eadweard; Date made=1885-07-06; ID Number=PG.003856.0130. Additionally, Catalog number=3856.0130, Accession number=98473, and Maker number=1084 exist, each serving different purposes.

## Step 04 · Restore the complete cyanotype original plate and corresponding image service

Action: Follow sequences/canvases/images in the Manifest to locate the same media object; open the full master image rather than the input cropped fragment.

Evidence observation: The media ID is SIA-2004-44757; the canvas width is 3276 and height is 1992. The resource provides the complete IIIF image, and direct download also retains the same master image; both are used to verify the overall layout. The Open Access statement is used to explain the official media source and does not replace the image itself.

## Step 05 · Exclude published editions of the same subject and other viewpoints

Action: Read the Description in the Manifest, then compare the complete plate header and the layout of side-view versus front/rear-view images.

Evidence observation: The institution's note states the cyanotype is a working contact print; published collotypes may have undergone cropping, reduction, or plate substitution; the related published object nmah_1885908 cannot directly replace this original plate. The header "8 Lat'ls" limits the count to eight side-view images; the 12 frames on the right represent other viewpoints and are not included in the denominator.

https://ids.si.edu/ids/download?id=SIA-2004-44757.jpg
https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/object/nmah_1885908

Result of this step: The closed scope includes only the eight side-view thumbnails, not all figure frames on the entire plate.

## Step 06 · Establish frame-by-frame ordering and a unified airborne criterion

Action: Number from left to right in the top row, then left to right in the bottom row; first locate the toes, heels, and ground line, then judge the gap between the outlines of both feet.

Evidence observation: Top row L01–L04, bottom row L05–L08. Both feet must be clearly separated from the ground line; obvious leg lifting, body tilt, or one foot suspended is insufficient. Dark areas where confirmation is impossible are excluded per the question rules; one cannot imagine gaps obscured by motion stages.

Evidence links:
https://ids.si.edu/ids/download?id=SIA-2004-44757.jpg

Result of this step: Provide yes/no for each frame and retain the reasons for exclusions.

## Step 07 · Frame-by-frame check L01

Action: Return to the corresponding position on the complete original plate and match it with the preserved crop of that frame; zoom in to view only existing outlines, without redrawing feet.

Evidence observation: The visible outlines of both feet are separated from the ground line, and gaps can be identified for each; do not misjudge ground contact because the entire figure is close to the bottom edge of the image.

## Step 13 · Frame-by-frame check L07

Action: Return to the corresponding position on the complete original plate and match it with the preserved crop of that frame; zoom in to view only existing outlines, without redrawing feet.

Evidence observation: Both feet are clearly suspended above the ground; gaps between the visible outlines and the ground line are distinguishable for each.

## Step 14 · Frame-by-frame check L08

Action: Return to the corresponding position on the complete original plate and match it with the preserved crop of that frame; zoom in to view only existing outlines, without redrawing feet.

Evidence observation: Both feet are visibly off the ground, satisfying the airborne condition; do not automatically treat the last frame in the sequence as a landing action.

Evidence links:
https://ids.si.edu/ids/download?id=SIA-2004-44757.jpg
https://ids.si.edu/ids/iiif/SIA-2004-44757/full/full/0/default.jpg

Result of this step: Airborne: Yes.

## Step 15 · Re-examine two easily confused negative cases

Action: Re-examine the feet and ground line in L03 and L04, and compare them with the clear gaps in L01/L02.

Evidence observation: L03 merely has a larger motion amplitude; L04 shows a dark outline contacting the ground; neither satisfies the requirement for both feet being clearly off the ground. The archive contains a first round of frame-by-frame judgments, but there is no record of a completed independent second annotation; this step does not describe the original labels as newly added independent blind reviews.

Evidence links:
https://ids.si.edu/ids/download?id=SIA-2004-44757.jpg

Result of this step: Maintain four YES and four NO.

## Step 16 · Summarize hits and calculate the proportion

Action: Extract YES entries in numerical order, then recalculate the denominator and percentage.

Evidence observation: YES=L01, L02, L07, L08; NO=L03, L04, L05, L06. All eight frames have been judged, 4+4=8; 4÷8=0.5=50%. The 12 frames on the right were never included in the denominator.

Evidence links:
https://ids.si.edu/ids/download?id=SIA-2004-44757.jpg

Result of this step: For Question 2, the answer is four numbers, 4 frames, and 50%.

## Step 17 · Verify question requirements and output scope

Action: Correspond each public required item one-by-one with the evidence above, checking the total set count, positive/negative items, and field formats.

Evidence observation: For Question 1, retain the formal title, author, production date, and ID Number; for Question 2, provide only the hit numbers, count, and proportion, without adding statistics for other perspectives not requested by the question.

Result of this step: Write only the requested information into the final answer; keep the search process and exclusion basis in the trajectory.

## Step 18 · Final Answer

(1) Work Title: Jumping, running, broad jump; Author: Eadweard Muybridge; Production Date: 1885-07-06; Collection Number: PG.003856.0130.

(2) The airborne frames are L01, L02, L07, and L08, totaling 4 frames, which accounts for 4/8 of all side-view thumbnails, i.e., 50%.
